successors.name: Hafsid dynasty
successors.text: Tripoli: 'He returned and finally captured the city in 1401'; 'Their rule definitely ended with the Hafsid reconquest of the city in 1401'

ledger.x: c. 1324: Thabit ibn 'Ammar takes power in Tripoli. He 'took power in the city toward 1324' and was murdered six months later; Muhammad's command began in 1326-1327, 'when the local population gave him control of the city'. The family governed 'nominally on behalf of the Hafsids' (Tripoli came under Hafsid authority…

wars.name: Genoese capture of Tripoli
wars.outcome: The Genoese captured Tripoli in 1354-1355; Thabit and his brother were killed by the Awlad Margham; the Genoese gave the city to the Banu Makki of Gabès for a large payment.

wars.name: Banu Thabit against the Banu Makki
Hafsid campaigns against Tripoli
wars.outcome: The Hafsid attack of 1392-1393 failed, with some Arab tribal support; Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz II arrested Ali in 1397-1398; the Hafsids captured the city in 1401.

certainty.note: The page names Tripoli only; the 50 km circle is the researcher's, and 1354-1368 has no shape.
